summary: security checked in 2 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release approvals and provenance, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 37 pass, 15 fail, and 7 unknown, with banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings open. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded reversible growth. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates; permit only reversible growth that does not add credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, cross-site behavior, or new exposure; continue existing read-only security evidence work only. Do not access credentials or private containers, modify permissions or configuration, deploy, requeue, add dependencies, or conduct external outreach.

Retain the existing bounded fleet security evidence matrix and do not create duplicate requests or production work. Record dated, redacted evidence, affected scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. No clean bill of health or certification is supported by the available data.
